summary: Established a site-to-site IPsec tunnel between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) carrying lan-a (10.10.1.0/24, node3) and lan-b (10.10.2.0/24, node4) over the transit network (10.10.3.0/24). Configured static addressing on the four routed interfaces, static routes on node3/node4, an IKEv2 tunnel (AES256/SHA256/MODP2048, PSK auth) using each vendor's native config surface (VyOS `set vpn ipsec` CLI; OPNsense config.xml Swanctl/IPsec model plus enc0 pseudo-interface registration and firewall pass rules), and verified encrypted end-to-end reachability between node3 and node4's private addresses. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery (interfaces, IPsec SA, firewall, cross-tunnel ping) at each step.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS (eth0 mgmt, eth1 transit, eth2 lan-a), node2=OPNsense (vtnet0 mgmt, vtnet1/opt1 transit, vtnet2/opt2 lan-b), node3/node4=Ubuntu 16.04 (ens2 mgmt, ens7 lan link)
Empirically determined physical interface mapping via ARP/neighbor discovery and ping tests

Assigned static IPs: lan-a 10.10.1.0/24 (node1 eth2 / node3 ens7), transit 10.10.3.0/24 (node1 eth1 / node2 opt1), lan-b 10.10.2.0/24 (node2 opt2 / node4 ens7); persisted via VyOS commit/save and Ubuntu /etc/network/interfaces
Added static routes on node3 (10.10.2.0/24 via 10.10.1.1) and node4 (10.10.1.0/24 via 10.10.2.1), persisted in /etc/network/interfaces

Configured VyOS site-to-site IPsec (ike-group, esp-group with PFS, authentication psk, site-to-site peer with tunnel local/remote prefixes) via native set vpn ipsec CLI, resolving 2026-rolling syntax differences by inspecting VyOS config templates

Configured OPNsense IPsec via config.xml edits to OPNsense.Swanctl (Connection/local/remote/child) and OPNsense.IPsec.preSharedKeys, matching VyOS's IKEv2/AES256/SHA256/MODP2048 proposal and tunnel selectors
Discovered and fixed that OPNsense's enc0 pseudo-interface must be registered via pluginctl -i before firewall rules referencing it compile; added pass rules for enc0, opt1, opt2
Verified IPsec SA established on both ends and confirmed via tcpdump that only ESP traverses the transit link between node1 and node2
Verified bidirectional ping between node3 (10.10.1.2) and node4 (10.10.2.2) succeeds through the encrypted tunnel
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, interface state, IPsec/route state) on all four nodes
Restarted node3, node4, node1, then node2 one at a time using each OS's native reboot mechanism, polling until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot identity on every node post-restart
Verified full recovery per node: persisted interface config, static routes, VyOS/OPNsense IPsec auto-reconnect, OPNsense firewall rules, and end-to-end encrypted ping between node3 and node4

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 carrying both private networks
evidence.summary: VyOS and OPNsense IPsec configs applied; swanctl shows ESTABLISHED IKEv2 SA and INSTALLED tunnel child SA with local/remote selectors 10.10.1.0/24 and 10.10.2.0/24 on both ends

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by private addresses
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping between node3 (10.10.1.2) and node4 (10.10.2.2) succeeds with 0% loss after full tunnel setup

evidence.requirement: Traffic is encrypted in transit across the transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface (eth1) during test pings shows only ESP packets between 10.10.3.1 and 10.10.3.2 on the wire; plaintext ICMP only appears as post-decryption capture on the receiving host, not as separate wire traffic

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2674ee60...; reboot acked; connection timed out confirming disconnection; boot_id changed to 6c5d5e63...; IPsec SA re-ESTABLISHED and tunnel INSTALLED automatically; node3->node4 ping succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 14:11:44; reboot triggered; connection timed out confirming disconnection; kern.boottime changed to 14:24:19; interfaces, IPsec SA (ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED), and enc0 firewall rules all recovered from persisted config.xml; node3->node4 ping succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 (Ubuntu) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9094f607...; reboot triggered; SSH connection refused confirming disconnection; boot_id changed to a70b78e9...; ens7 static IP persisted from /etc/network/interfaces and cross-tunnel ping to node4 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node4 (Ubuntu) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a1dc8e25...; reboot triggered; SSH connection refused confirming disconnection; boot_id changed to bf0fab4d...; ens7 static IP persisted and cross-tunnel ping to node3 succeeded
